key_insight: Finite-point interpolation and transport-map approximation provide criteria for distributional universality, including Wasserstein universality of affine-invariant vector-field families containing a non-affine field.
engineering_relevance: The results guide the design of expressive neural ODE generators by connecting vector-field capabilities to the probability distributions their flows can approximate.
method: Quantitatively relate finite-sample point interpolation to Wasserstein approximation.
Derive universality criteria from L^p approximation of transport maps.
Combine one-dimensional Sobolev approximation with shear-type mixing for total variation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical bounds and universality results, not datasets or empirical benchmarks.
watch_item: Universality depends on assumptions such as compactly supported, absolutely continuous base measures; coordinate-wise dynamics alone are insufficient for total-variation universality in dimensions d ≥ 2.
paper_title: Point interpolation and distributional universality in flow-based generative models
